result.title: The Show-Up Attack: When Subagents Win Over Their Supervisor
result.summary: Multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed to coordinate multiple large language model (LLM) agents. However, this also creates new attack surfaces: malicious agents may have chances to exploit the coordination. In this paper, we propose and study the \textit{show-up attack}, in which a malicious subagent manipulates the supervisor into involving it in tasks beyond its assigned scope. To evaluate this risk, we propose SUA-Arena, which implements 6 attack strategies and contains 188 test cases. Then, we evaluate 6 frontier LLMs and find that all of them are vulnerable to show-up attacks. For example, GPT-5.6-Sol as a supervisor suffers an ASR of up to 0.93. Mitigation strategies such as prompting and restricted communication fail to reduce the risk consistently. These results show that multi-agent systems need explicit mechanisms for enforcing authority boundaries.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出并研究「show-up attack」：恶意子智能体诱导 supervisor 在超出其被指派范围的任务中调用自己；作者构建 SUA-Arena（6 种攻击策略、188 个测试用例）评测 6 个前沿 LLM，发现均存在漏洞，且 prompting、限制通信等缓解手段效果不稳定。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作聚焦多智能体协作中的越权调用与对抗安全，未涉及视觉细节保留、latent 推理状态生成、证据筛选或停止决策，未提供可核查的 LVR 方法借鉴线索。
